reproduction_status: not reproduced; records describe what the page shows
notes: Nineteen numbered figures, two tables, one unnumbered memorandum diagram, one unnumbered memorandum chart, and two appendix tables. Figures 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10 were read by the root from page proxies; the rest were read from crops by a read-only subagent and returned as text. Tables 1 and 2 were read from the text layer.

visualization_observations.analytical_purpose: Show the two raw price series before any processing, so the reader sees the scale difference the normalization later removes.
visualization_observations.summary: Caption 'Figure 1: The daily asset prices'. Two panels, '(a) gold' titled 'Gold daily prices' and '(b) bitcoin' titled 'Bitcoin daily prices'. No axis titles. Gold y-ticks 1300, 1500, 1800, 2000 (the 1600 tick is not clearly printed), bitcoin y-ticks 0, 20k, 40k, 60k, both x-axes years 2017-2021. Gold is a jagged orange line near 1200-1300 through 2019, rising to a peak near 2000 around 2020, then easing. Bitcoin stays near the baseline with a small bump near 2018, then spikes above 60k in 2021 and pulls back. No point markers.
visualization_observations.exact_claim_supported: The raw series are not comparable: gold moves inside roughly 1200-2000 while bitcoin runs from near zero to above 60k, which is why section 3.3 normalizes.
visualization_observations.missing_or_unverified: The 1600 gold tick is not clearly printed; axis titles are absent.

visualization_observations.analytical_purpose: Show both return distributions are sharply centered at zero before the stationarity argument.
visualization_observations.summary: Caption 'Figure 2: Histogram of the return distribution'. Panel (a) gold_return spans x from -0.04 to 0.04 with y up to 100; panel (b) bitcoin_return spans x from -0.2 to 0.2 with y up to 200. Both spike at zero.
visualization_observations.exact_claim_supported: Bitcoin's daily moves are about five times wider than gold's, and both returns pile up at zero.
visualization_observations.missing_or_unverified: Bin counts were read from the axis scale, not from a data table.

visualization_observations.analytical_purpose: Justify differencing by showing the autocorrelation dies after the first difference.
visualization_observations.summary: Caption 'Figure 3: ACF inspection chart'. Three panels, x from 0 to 20. (a) acf_normal decays slowly from 1.0 inside a shaded band; (b) acf_differ1 and (c) acf_differ2 sit near zero inside narrow bands.
visualization_observations.exact_claim_supported: The level series is autocorrelated; the first and second differences are not, so one difference is enough.
visualization_observations.missing_or_unverified: The shaded band bounds were read as drawn, not checked against a formula.

visualization_observations.analytical_purpose: Show how gold's missing market days are filled, so the reader sees the rule rather than only reading it.
visualization_observations.summary: Caption 'Figure 4: Handling the missing values'. One row of cells 'a b c d NAN ...... NAN NAN e f g' with an arrow rising from each NAN to a cell labeled 'd'.
visualization_observations.exact_claim_supported: Missing values are forward-filled with the last valid value, here 'd'.
visualization_observations.missing_or_unverified: None.

visualization_observations.analytical_purpose: Make the lag visible so the cointegration test that follows has something to confirm.
visualization_observations.summary: Caption 'Figure 5: Observation of price correlation'. No axis titles. Y-ticks only 0 and 2, x-ticks 2017-2021. Legend orange 'BTC', blue 'Gold'. A left-side y-tick above 2 is cut off. The word 'lag' is also bold in the prose above the figure.

visualization_observations.analytical_purpose: Show the leakage safeguard and the model the baselines use, before any result is claimed.
visualization_observations.summary: Caption 'Figure 9: Data split and Model structure'. visualization_observations.analytical_purpose: Show the tracking error over time so the prose can dismiss the 2017 spike as one period.
visualization_observations.summary: Caption 'Figure 11: The (yearly) tracking error of four different strategies'. No axis titles. Years 2016-2021, y from about -1.00 to 4.50 in steps of 0.50. Legend stochastic simulation (orange), Pair Trade (green), XGBoost (gold), LSTM (brown). All four peak in 2017: stochastic near 4, XGBoost and LSTM near 3.5, Pair Trade near 1.5. All fall to about 0 in 2018; Pair Trade then rises to roughly 1.5 by 2020 while the others stay under 1.

visualization_observations.analytical_purpose: Show return against time for ten cost rates so the cost effect is a family of curves.
visualization_observations.summary: Caption 'Figure 15: The return of the model under differnt transaction costs', with 'differnt' printed. Internal title spells 'different' correctly. X years 2017-2021, y-ticks 0, 20k, 40k, 60k, 80k, 100k, 120k. Legend from darkest to lightest red: broke_0, broke_0.001, broke_0.005, broke_0.01, broke_0.02, broke_0.03, broke_0.05, broke_0.08, broke_0.1, broke_0.2. All lines stay low until 2021, then rise, and the higher cost ends lower.

visualization_observations.missing_or_unverified: The zero-cost line's endpoint was not read as exactly 120k.

visualization_observations.analytical_purpose: Give the cost effect a closed form and a fitted curve.
visualization_observations.summary: Caption 'Figure 16: Sensitivity analysis of transaction costs'. Panel (a) 'Relationship between transaction times and transaction discount': a green decay from 1 toward 0 over n from 0 to 500, with a box reading a_n/a_0=(1+0.01)^n. Panel (b) 'Fitting curve for brokerage and return': orange 'fitted_curve' and blue 'true_values' both fall from about 100k to near 0 as brokerage alpha goes from 0 to 0.2. The boxed formula reads a_n=a_0(1 - alpha*k/(1+alpha))^25.
visualization_observations.exact_claim_supported: Panel (b)'s box uses k, the same symbol as equation (33), and an exponent of 25 rather than n.
visualization_observations.missing_or_unverified: The exponent 25 is printed but not explained on the figure.
